 East Bengal’s Knockout Hopes Hang in Balance After Defeat to Hwacheon KSPO
 A Draw in Group A Could Seal East Bengal’s Quarter-Final Berth. 
 Goal Difference Could Prove Decisive as Bam Khatoon and Ayeyawady Fight for Survival. By Somnath Roy November 5, 2026 No Comments 2 Mins Read

 East Bengal FC suffered a 4-1 defeat against Korea Republic’s Hwacheon KSPO WFC in their second AFC Women’s Champions League match in Kolkata. However, the Moshal Girls still have a chance of qualifying for the quarter-finals, with their hopes of progressing hinging on the final round of group-stage matches on Saturday.
 East Bengal had held the Korean champions to a 1-1 draw at half-time but struggled to contain Hwacheon in the second half, conceding three goals. The result leaves both teams on three points, with East Bengal currently third in Group B with a goal difference of -2.
 However, East Bengal’s qualification scenario could become much simpler depending on Saturday’s Group A fixture between Iran’s Bam Khatoon FC and Myanmar’s Ayeyawady FC. Both teams are yet to open their accounts after losing their first two matches and will face each other in their final group-stage fixture.
 In case of a draw, East Bengal will qualify for the quarter-finals, irrespective of the result between them and 4.25 SC of DPR Korea. In that case, neither Bam Khatoon nor Ayeyawady can move past East Bengal in the standings, making goal difference irrelevant.
 However, if either team wins, the margin of victory will be key. East Bengal need the winning side to win by a margin of no more than three goals to keep their mathematical hopes of qualification alive. East Bengal also need to avoid a heavy defeat against 4.25 SC, losing by no more than three goals, to stay ahead on goal difference.
 East Bengal currently have a goal difference of -2, which is well ahead of Bam Khatoon’s -8 and Ayeyawady’s -9. If there is a winner in the Group A fixture, that could prove a telling advantage.
 East Bengal will play their final group-stage match against 4.25 SC on Saturday. They still have a chance to progress, either by finishing in the top two or as one of the two best third-placed teams across the groups, with the North Korean side already assured of one of the two automatic qualification spots.
 For the Moshal Girls, Saturday could offer a straightforward path to qualification even before they take the field. A draw between Bam Khatoon and Ayeyawady would guarantee them a quarter-final place and allow them to play their final match without the anxiety of needing another result to go their way.
